analysis:
Examined three changed files.

1) ProviderLoop+PrefetchPublication.swift head:25 makes selfTestRecordRefuses non-private (visibility only; logic unchanged). head:48 adds beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence(modelId), whose implementation is not supplied. head:263-265 adds verified builds to autopilotInventoryModels when joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified(info) holds. This runs only after all fail-closed guards: non-empty weight hash (111), self-test record (123, 244), CBv2 support (140), retirement (158, 243), autopilotAllowsModel and capacity (175, 223). The weight hash is still recorded in modelHashes/liveModelHashes, and models_update still carries the hash for the coordinator catalog cross-check (T-012/T-027). No weakening of attestation or weight-hash binding is visible.

2) ProviderLoop+Preload.swift head:30 replaces autopilotAllowsModel with autopilotServesModel in the coordinator load_model gate. This only selects which models are allowed to load; the coordinator is trusted. Runtime eligibility, shutdown, revision and drain checks are unchanged. head:119 makes finishPreloadTask non-private. Its taskId guard is retained.

3) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift head:289 starts startAutopilotCandidateVerification. head:477-480 shuts down autopilotDownloadCoordinator and cancels the verification task on shutdown, which helps availability.

Open questions for integration (implementations not in this batch):
- Whether autopilotServesModel is at least as strict as autopilotAllowsModel, for example consent and catalog membership.
- Whether joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified requires saved consent and coordinator catalog membership.
- Whether the autopilot download coordinator and candidate verification enforce aggregate hash verification before calling publishVerifiedPrefetch. This is especially relevant for the verifiedArtifact path at line 76, which skips local re-hashing.
- What beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence does.

These are not proven regressions. They are recorded here rather than as findings.
